messages:
Nina (eng): Hey people-ops — noticed my payroll portal shows both a W-2 and a 1099 for 2025. I was converted from contractor to full-time in Aug 2025. Can someone help reconcile? cc @Sara (People Ops).
Sara (People Ops): Hi Nina — sorry about that. Can you DM me the paystub screenshots and the last 4 of your SSN? Please do NOT post PII in channel.
Dan (Payroll): @Sara I'll take this. Nina, do you have the payrun ids or dates? Need to confirm if any contractor invoices were paid after transfer date. If there's overlap, we may need to issue a 1099-NEC correction and a W-2c. Provider: Rippling. Timeline ~7-14 business days after we file.
Nina (eng): DM'd the screenshots and payrun dates. One invoice on 2025-08-15 and salary effective 2025-08-01 — so looks like overlap on Aug 15.
Ben (Manager): Nina, sorry for the confusion — I approved the contractor payout before HR confirmed the start date. My mistake, will coordinate with finance to reverse.
Dan (Payroll): Thanks. Quick checklist: 1) Confirm invoice amounts & dates. 2) Check if contractor payout triggered 1099 issuance. 3) If duplicate, process a W-2c + corrected 1099-NEC. Nina: expected outcome — you'll receive corrected tax docs; if any extra tax withheld we can advise on withholding adjustments or reimbursements. Target to submit filings by 2026-01-12.
Sara (People Ops): Also flag: contractor payment was tagged CA, but your residency on file is NY since July 2025 — that changes state tax reporting. Please confirm primary state.
Nina (eng): Confirmed — primary is NY as of 2025-07-10.
Dan (Payroll): Noted. If CA withholding occurred, we can file for CA withholding refund and reallocate to NY on the corrected W-2. CA processing can add extra time. We'll keep you updated.
PayrollBot (Rippling): Payroll run 2025-08-15 id=`pr_88234` shows manual contractor payout processed (amount masked).
Sara (People Ops): Action items: @Dan file W-2c + 1099 correction; @Finance confirm reversal/ledger entry for contractor payout; @Nina confirm preference for handling withholding (refund vs net adjustment). I'll follow up in DM for PII and to confirm timelines.
Nina (eng): Prefer a refund for the withholding error, thanks :pray:.
Dan (Payroll): Noted. I'll update this thread once filings are submitted. ETA ~2 weeks for submission, then processing time varies.
